title: Can Taste Become Institutional Knowledge?
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: Taste becomes institutional knowledge only when people can examine how a judgment was made, practice it, dispute it, preserve its context, and retain authority over what may be carried.
Dress is retained as additional official resource located during the dated excavation pass.
narrativeSequence.rights: Public Domain under Met Open Access; exact image installed separately.

narrativeSequence.caption: 01 · ELICIT — What happened before “I just knew”?. Reconstruct the comparison set, sensory cue, memory, technical constraint, cultural reference, commercial condition, and rejected alternative. Record uncertainty and the contributor who supplied each part of the judgment.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · DEMONSTRATE — Can the judgment be shown in context?. Pair expert demonstration with a learner attempt, correction, second attempt, and commentary on acceptable variation. Some knowledge is tactile, temporal, embodied, confidential, or culturally governed; not everything belongs on camera.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · CONTEST — Who can say the founder is wrong?. Create a review ritual where pattern, textile, production, wearer, commercial, cultural, accessibility, and archive perspectives can challenge a choice. Preserve the reason for override rather than manufacturing consensus.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · GOVERN — Who may retain and teach it?. Attach consent, compensation, attribution, confidentiality, access, teaching, archive, withdrawal, and cultural-authority fields. Keep protected expression, contract rights, trade secrets, know-how, and abstract taste as separate questions.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
